title: Kaagaz 42 Baar Fold Karo, Chaand Tak Pahunch Jaoge!
idea: A sheet of paper 0.1 mm thick that doubles with every fold would pass the Burj Khalifa at 23 folds and Everest at 27 folds, and would go past the Moon at 42 folds.

lines.text: Ek kaagaz ko sirf 42 baar fold karo, woh Chaand tak pahunch jaayega!
Kaagaz sirf 0.1 mm mota hota hai, par har fold pe double!
Sirf 23 fold mein 839 metre, Burj Khalifa se bhi uncha!
27 fold pe 13 km, Mount Everest bhi chhota pad gaya!
Aur 42 fold pe 4.4 lakh km, Chaand sirf 3.84 lakh km door hai!
Par asli duniya ka record sirf 12 fold hai, aap kitne kar paoge?

facts.claim: A 0.1 mm sheet doubles in thickness with each fold, so its thickness is 0.1 × 2^n mm. At 42 folds that is about 439,805 km, which is more than the roughly 384,400 km to the Moon.
42 folds is the first whole number of folds that reaches the Moon's distance (n ≈ 41.8).
23 folds: 0.1 mm × 2^23 ≈ 839 m, which is taller than the Burj Khalifa's official 828 m.
27 folds: 0.1 mm × 2^27 ≈ 13.4 km, which is taller than Everest's official 8,848.86 m (about 1.5×).
Britney Gallivan set the well-known paper-folding record of 12 folds in 2002 using a very long roll of paper.
Scientific American explains how folding a sheet of paper could, in theory, reach the Moon.
